title: Dementia in elderly male with Stiff man syndrome

C14
Dementia in elderly male with Stiff Man Syndrome.
I.
Sheyner,M .Cutillar. Internal Medicine, University of South
Florida, Tampa, FL.
Abstract:
We are presenting the case of a 75 year old male undergoing
long term care in the nursing home with a past medical history of
Stiffman syndrome diagnosed seventeen years ago. Diagnosis was
based on clinical observation and had recently been confirmed by a
positive anti-glutamic acid decarboxylase antibody. On admission, the
chief complaint was stiffness of the right leg with episodic spasms in-
duced by voluntary movements and frequent falls. Additionally, the
family reported recent worsening in the patient’s short term memory.
After complete medical evaluation the patient was diagnosed with
mild dementia, Stiffman syndrome and deconditioning which led to
frequent falls. Treatment with diazepam and several sessions of
plasmapharesis provided reasonable control of symptoms. Treatment
was complicated by occasional episodes of delirium which were man-
aged by careful titration of benzodiazepines.
Stiffman syndrome(SMS) is a disorder characterized by pro-
gressive muscle rigidity and painful reflex spasms involving the axial
and limb muscles. Continuous contraction of agonist and antagonist
muscles caused by involuntary motor-unit firing at rest are the hall-
mark clinical and electrophysiologic signs of the disease. Diagnosis is
also supported by a positive anti-glutamic acid decarboxylase anti-
body. The cornerstone of therapy is administration of benzodi-
azepines, which are thought to modulate the level and activity of
gamma-amino butyric acid(GABA). Plasmapharesis may be an op-
tion in patients who exhibit minimal improvement on high doses of
benzodiazepines.
SMS is a rare disease which is challenging in diagnosis and treat-
ment. We are reporting a finding of dementia developing in the set-
ting of SMS, and present the challenging details of diagnosis and
treatment.
